entities.mathematical concept: A defined mathematical term that is not a distribution family, construction or parameter: the gamma function, the standard score, the moment generating function. Examples: the gamma function; the standard score.
entities.distribution family: A named family of probability distributions, possibly with parameters: the normal distribution, the gamma distribution, the standard normal distribution. Mentions include adjectival forms ("normally distributed", "has a gamma distribution"). Examples: the normal distribution; lognormal distribution; normally distributed.
entities.family construction: A way of generating a family of distributions from a base distribution, such as the location-scale family, the location family or the scale family associated with a distribution, or the general exponential family. Not itself a single distribution family. Examples: location-scale family; scale family associated with the given distribution.
entities.distribution parameter: A parameter of a distribution family or construction, such as the location parameter, the scale parameter, the shape parameter k, the rate, the mean or the standard deviation when these parameterize the family. Examples: location parameter; shape parameter k; the rate parameter.
entities.random variable: A random variable denoted by a symbol (X, Y, Z, X_1, W) or by an expression in other random variables (a + b X, e^Y, X_1 + X_2). Local to the statement or section that introduces it. Examples: X; a + b X; X_1 + X_2.

labels.asserted: Concluded or stated as true; structural claims.
labels.supposed: A supposition: suppose, assume, if, or let about something taken as given.
labels.defined: What a definition stipulates, including a formula introducing a variable.
labels.exemplified: Setup values in examples and exercises.
labels.posed: Reserved until an asks_for predicate exists (OPEN-D2-15).

labels.corollary: A result stated to follow from another.
labels.example: A worked example with setup values.
labels.exercise: An exercise with setup values and an asked quantity.
labels.assumption: A statement whose only content is a supposition (a context premise).
labels.narrative: Narrative text between units that states claims.

has distribution.description: The random variable has a distribution in the family, optionally with stated parameter values. "X is normally distributed with mean μ and variance σ²".

has parameter.description: A family or construction has this parameter. "with shape parameter k and scale parameter b".
